note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

compliance.verdict: The item mostly holds up under the compliance lens, but it is not fully clean: one medium and three low findings remain. All of these I confirmed: my re-run of ./gb tier-f gates passes all five gates and writes a gates.json identical to the author's. The checks: solvability 10/10, 724 tokens, 3/3 variants reach V6, start fails at V6 (f2p fails, p2p passes), and 9/9 mutants are valid and killed. A copy of build.py run in scratch regenerates task.json, start.grc, reference.grc and all three variants byte for byte. The seed filter/polyphase_channelizer_demo.grc is test-split, and its sha256 (8bce36c1...) matches the installed example and the inventory. The licence, source, cluster_id, provenance and review fields are correct. The perturbation record matches the seed (32000, 0.03/0.38/0.70*samp_rate, amplitudes 1, noise .01). No model-visible file contains the canary. reports/reference/training_task_specs.json has no channelizer task, and no other item uses this seed. The level is L2 (12 functional blocks, with a rate change and filtering). The tolerances leave comfortable margin (peak errors of 5-6 Hz against a 26.8 Hz tolerance; rms within 0.5 %). The 9 listed mutants all break the spec. My probes found no liveness or false-negative risk for legitimate sharp-filter solutions (filters down to a 100 Hz transition band pass). The problems: (F1, medium) the stated pass-to-pass requirement 'keep the noise (amplitude 0.02)' is measurable but unchecked, so removing the noise or changing it 2.5-3.5x passes. (F2, low) the filtering wording is unsatisfiable, and the reference and variants each contradict it. (F3, low) the 48 kHz sample rate, and with it the samp_rate perturbation, cannot be observed (samp_rate 12000 or 32000 passes). (F4, low) channel 2's 12 kHz rate is unchecked. Probe files and results are in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-16/muts/ (probe_results.json); the regenerated copy is in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-16/regen/. The only thing I changed in the task directory is gates.json, which the gate run rewrote with identical content.

findings.claim: The p2p requirement 'keep the noise (complex Gaussian, amplitude 0.02)' is measurable but not checked. A solution that deletes the noise source, sets its amplitude to 0, raises it to 0.05 or 0.07, or switches it to uniform noise passes all 12 V6 checks. The only check that involves noise is ch2 rms with max 0.05 and no lower bound, so it tests that tones are absent, not that the noise is still there.
findings.evidence: I built probe flowgraphs from reference.grc and ran ladder.check with the task's oracle (scratch ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-16/muts/, probe_results.json). All reached V6 and passed both p2p and f2p. The ch2 rms values were: reference 0.0112; noise amp 0 → 5e-06; noise source and throttle deleted with add num_inputs 3 → 5e-06; amp 0.05 → 0.028; amp 0.07 → 0.039; GR_UNIFORM → 0.0066. The spectrum.dat checks barely move: rms 0.9908-0.9936 against 0.9902 ±5 %, and the band fractions stay inside ±10 %, because noise power (4e-4) is 0.04 % of the total. The instruction says 'Keep everything else as it is: ... the noise', and spec_properties[0] claims 'plus noise of amplitude 0.02'. The only noise mutant listed is amp 0.5 (25x), which is easy to kill.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the ch2 rms on both sides so it checks the noise level. Valid designs I measured give 0.0086-0.0122 (reference 0.011, v1/v2-style filters about 0.0097), so for example min 0.005 and max 0.025 would work. Then add mutants 'noise amp 0' and 'noise amp 0.05' (set_param on analog_noise_source_x_0) with breaks = the wideband/ch2 property. Either reword spec_properties to match what is checked, or accept that Gaussian vs uniform cannot be told apart and drop 'Gaussian' from the checked claim.

findings.claim: The filtering requirement in the instruction cannot be met as written. It asks for a brick wall: 'signals within 6 kHz of the channel centre keep their amplitude, and signals outside the channel are filtered out, as the current channelizer does'. Neither the reference nor the variants satisfy it, and 'as the current channelizer does' is false. Scoring is not affected, because the oracle only tests tones at most 1.92 kHz from a centre and at least 10.08 kHz away.
findings.evidence: I computed the frequency responses with the GR 3.10.12 Python. The reference prototype is optfir.low_pass(1, 4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.1, 100) with 82 taps. Its gain at offsets from a channel centre is 7.0 kHz +0.1 dB, 7.5 kHz -0.8 dB, 8.0 kHz -5.3 dB and 9.0 kHz -34 dB. So signals 6-8 kHz from the centre, which are outside the 12 kHz channel, pass almost unchanged and alias into the channel. The start graph's 3-channel filter passes up to 9.6 kHz at 0 dB with an 8 kHz channel half-width. The v2 taps (firdes.low_pass 5 kHz/2 kHz) give 5.0 kHz -6 dB and 6.0 kHz -26.7 dB. The v1 taps (low_pass_2 5 kHz/2 kHz/80 dB) give 5.0 kHz -6 dB and 6.0 kHz -60 dB. Both therefore violate 'within 6 kHz keep their amplitude'. Sharp-filter answers that try to follow the text still pass (firdes.low_pass(1, samp_rate, 5800, 100), 1584 taps, passes V6), so there is no false negative. But the item's own reference contradicts its instruction.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the requirement as what the oracle checks and every valid design achieves. For example: 'signals within 2 kHz of a channel centre keep their amplitude, and signals 10 kHz or more from the centre are removed'. Alternatively, keep the 'as the current channelizer does' wording and drop the 6 kHz claim. Also remove 'as the current channelizer does', since the current one does not filter out out-of-channel signals.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'Keep ... the 48 kHz sample rate' and states absolute tone frequencies (1.2 / 13.92 / 34.56 kHz), but the oracle cannot see either. Every tone is defined as a fraction of samp_rate, so changing samp_rate scales all frequencies together and the measurements look the same. As a result, the sample-rate perturbation (32000 → 48000) has no effect on scoring. A model that misreads '12 kHz' and sets samp_rate=12000, which puts the tones at 300 Hz, 3.48 kHz and 8.64 kHz, passes. The author notes this, but it can be fixed cheaply.
findings.evidence: Probes samp_rate_32000 (the original example's value) and samp_rate_12000 both pass V6, and every check value is identical to the reference: spectrum peak 1218.75, ch0 1205.36 Hz/0.7967, ch3 -1446.43 Hz/0.2985, and so on. task.json notes: 'samp_rate itself is not observable in the samples (all tone frequencies are fractions of samp_rate), so no mutant changes it.' The perturbation record still lists samp_rate 32000→48000 as a change 'so memorized answers fail'.
findings.suggested_fix: In the start graph, give the tone frequencies as absolute Hz values ('1200', '13920', '34560') instead of fractions of samp_rate. This is still a valid perturbation. A samp_rate change then moves the channel grid and channel rates relative to the tones, which the existing peak_freq checks catch. Add a mutant samp_rate=32000 with breaks = the wideband property. If you keep the current design, drop the sample-rate change from the perturbation's anti-memorisation rationale.

findings.claim: The instruction says 'Each channel output must be a complex stream at 12 kHz', but channel 2's rate is never checked. spec_properties for ch2 leave out the rate, and the only ch2 check is rms ≤ 0.05. A solution whose ch2.dat is at 48 kHz (not decimated) passes.
findings.evidence: In probe v2_ch2_decim1 (variant v2 with xlate_ch2 decim set to 1, so ch2.dat runs at 48 kHz), V6 passes in both groups with ch2 rms 0.0086. In task.json, spec_properties[3] is 'ch2.dat: channel 2 ... contains none of the tones ... only noise'; the 12 kHz rate is listed for ch0, ch1 and ch3 only. The rate can be measured through the noise shape. At 12 kHz the in-channel noise is roughly flat across ±6 kHz. At 48 kHz with a channel filter, all the noise falls in the centre quarter, so band_fraction(ch2, fs=12000, -3000, 3000) is about 1.0 instead of about 0.5-0.7.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a ch2 band_fraction check (fs 12000, lo -3000, hi 3000, max about 0.85) with the rate added to the ch2 spec property, or place a weak tone (for example 0.1 at 25 kHz) in channel 2 and check its offset like the others. Otherwise, state in the notes that the ch2 rate is deliberately left unchecked.

item-quality.verdict:
The task is not acceptable yet. Three findings survive; one of them wrongly rejects correct answers. Most of the item is sound. The seed is test-split and its sha256 matches. L2/modify is correct (12 functional blocks with a rate change), and every number in the instruction matches the graph. The start graph fails only the f2p group at V6, and all 9 mutants are real spec breaks and are killed. No canary appears in any .grc file.

1. HIGH. Correct answers built from standard FFT-based channel-selection blocks fail V5 liveness, some of them only on some runs. The cause is the 1024-item run length combined with the spectrum tap on the shared adder output.
2. MEDIUM. The instruction asks for a brick-wall channel filter and says the current channelizer already is one. The reference is not: a tone 7 kHz from a channel centre comes through at full amplitude.
3. MEDIUM. The p2p group does not check "keep ... the noise". A graph with the noise source deleted passes.
4. LOW. Discrimination: the instruction spells the edit out almost completely.

Changing the run to n_items=512 and adding a 0.005 noise floor on ch2 fixes findings 1 and 3. I checked this on scratch copies of the task: the reference, the 3 variants and 15 other correct answers pass, all 9 mutants are still killed, and the start graph still fails on f2p only.

Scratch files are in WSL ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-16/ (alternative answers *.grc, alt2/, alt3/, task_n512.json, task_n512_floor.json). The scripts are in C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\gbf16_*.py.

findings.claim: Correct answers that pick each channel out with a standard FFT-based block fail V5 liveness under the task's run settings (n_items = min_items = 1024). They fail on most runs, and one of them passes on some runs and fails on others. The oracle never sees their output, so correct answers are scored as wrong.
findings.evidence:
I wrote alternative answers in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-test-16 and ran each through ./gb ladder's check() with the task's own task.json:
- E_pfb_decimator.grc (4 Polyphase Decimators, decim 4, channel k, default FFT settings): V5 failed on 4 of 4 runs, e.g. "liveness: an observation point received too few items {'spectrum': 1024, 'ch0': 1008, 'ch1': 1008, ...}".
- alt2/I_rotator_fftfilter.grc (Rotator + fft_filter_xxx ccc, decim 4): failed on 4 of 4 runs.
- alt2/H_xlating_fft.grc (freq_xlating_fft_filter_ccc, decim 4): failed on 2 of 4 runs and passed V6 on the other 2, so the same answer gets different verdicts.

The three graphs are correct. With the spectrum point removed (task_nospectrum.json) all three pass V6, and with n_items=512 they pass V6 on 3 of 3 runs each.

Cause: the harness taps spectrum with Head(1024) on the adder output. Once that tap has its 1024 items it stops reading, so the shared adder buffer fills and stalls. The channel paths can then draw only about 1024 plus one buffer (roughly 5k) of input samples. Block-based FFT filters need more than 4096 inputs to emit 1024 outputs, so they get only 1008. build.py itself notes the margin is only about 25%. The committed variants (pfb_channelizer, FIR xlating filters, hier channelizer) all use non-FFT filtering, so the variants gate could not catch this.

findings.claim: The instruction's filter requirement is impossible as written, and the reference does not meet it either. The instruction says "signals within 6 kHz of the channel centre keep their amplitude, and signals outside the channel are filtered out, as the current channelizer does". With a 12 kHz output rate that is a brick wall at the channel edge. The start and reference channelizer (bw 0.6, tb 0.2) passes signals up to about 7.2 kHz from the centre and folds them back into the channel. The oracle only puts tones 1.2-1.92 kHz from a centre or more than 10.08 kHz away, so it never notices. The wording also pushes models toward very sharp filters, and the oracle wrongly rejects one such correct design.
findings.evidence:
gbf16_alias.py runs pfb.channelizer_hier_ccf(4, 4, None, None, 100, 0.6, 0.2, 0.1) at 48 kHz, as in the reference:
- A tone at +7000 Hz (outside channel 0's ±6 kHz) appears in ch0 with rms 1.006 at -5000 Hz.
- A tone at +7500 Hz appears in ch0 with rms 0.904.
- A tone at +5000 Hz (7 kHz below channel 1's centre) appears in ch1 with rms 1.006.
So "as the current channelizer does" is false.

A model that takes the brick-wall wording literally with C3_pfb_lp2_verysharp.grc (pfb_channelizer_ccf, taps firdes.low_pass_2(1, samp_rate, 5900, 100, 100), 2181 taps) is correct once the filter has settled. It still fails V6 with ch0 rms 0.733 vs 0.8, ch1 0.458 vs 0.5 and ch3 0.275 vs 0.3. Its start-up transient (a group delay of about 272 output items) is longer than the 128-item skip. A 1091-tap design (C_pfb_lp2_sharp.grc) passes, and a near-brick-wall hier setting (bw 0.495, tb 0.005) fails at V5 with remez "insufficient extremals".
findings.suggested_fix:
Rewrite the filter sentence so it is achievable, matches the reference and covers what the oracle checks. For example: "keep the channelizer's current filter settings; signals within 2 kHz of a channel centre must keep their amplitude, and signals more than 10 kHz away from a channel centre must be removed from that channel". Alternatively, state the prototype filter (bw 0.6 of a channel, transition 0.2, 100 dB) explicitly.

If the team keeps a looser wording, either add a check that shows the intended edge behaviour or remove the claim about the current channelizer. Also note in the oracle notes that rms checks assume a filter transient of 128 items or less.

findings.claim: The instruction states "Keep everything else as it is: ... the noise" (complex Gaussian, amplitude 0.02), but no check fails when the noise is removed or changed. The p2p group checks only tone features and total RMS, where noise power is 0.04% of the total, and the ch2 check is only rms ≤ 0.05.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "min": 0.005 to the ch2 rms check and name the noise in its "requires" text. A tight upper bound would wrongly reject correct answers whose filter width differs (v3 uses bw 0.4), so leave the 0.05 maximum as it is. Optionally, add a noise-removal mutant (e.g. set noise amp 0) to the mutations list.

findings.claim: The instruction spells out the solution almost completely, so the item may separate strong models from weak ones poorly. It gives the channel count and the channel-k-at-k×12 kHz numbering, which is the block's native order. It also says which output goes to which existing sink and that a new complex File Sink to ch3.dat is needed. The edit is then nchans: '4' plus one File Sink and one connection. build.py's docstring claims the model must "know how the channelizer numbers its channels (channel k centred on k*fs/N, so channel 3 is at -12 kHz)", but the instruction already gives that mapping.
findings.evidence: reference.grc differs from start.grc only by nchans: '4' on pfb_channelizer_hier_ccf_0, one blocks_file_sink (ch3_sink, complex, ch3.dat) and one connection [pfb_channelizer_hier_ccf_0, '3', ch3_sink, '0']. The instruction states the k×12 kHz centre map and the file assignment for all four channels.
findings.suggested_fix: This is a team decision; the item is not incorrect. If more discrimination is wanted, describe the channels by frequency in an order that differs from the native one. For example: "ch0.dat gets the channel centred on -12 kHz, ch1.dat on 0 Hz, ch2.dat on +12 kHz, ch3.dat on 24 kHz". The model then has to know the channelizer's output order (outchans, or rewiring). Re-run the gates afterwards and update the docstring's difficulty rationale either way.
